Foldes Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Földes, Hungary

Not demolished. Földes's first Jews are recorded in 1816; the Orthodox community, founded in the early 1800s, had a synagogue and mikveh by 1820, later adding a Talmud Torah and yeshiva. A new synagogue built in 1845 through community donations was expanded several times. During the 1848-49 War of Independence, 3 Jews served in the army; population fell to 78 by 1853 before recovering to 156 by 1861. Remaining Orthodox after 1871's Schism, the community ran an elementary school (closed in 1883 for lacking a certified teacher, then reopened) and by 1929 numbered 253 (60 families, 55 taxpayers) in trades including merchants, artisans, and one entrepreneur. Fifty members served in WWI, six dying; the community's Chevra Kadisha won Interior Ministry approval in 1898, and the villages of Sáp and Tetétlen fell under its jurisdiction. In WWII, 65 men were sent to forced labor (33 survived); the remaining 214 Jews were deported via the Püspökladány Ghetto to Debrecen and then Auschwitz in 1944. A 1990 memorial names 193 Holocaust victims; postwar survivors briefly rebuilt a 50-person community before near-total emigration left only 10 Jews by 1957, with the synagogue demolished the following year.
